positioning: Hotel 41: an intimate London hotel with the feel of a private members' club, steps from Buckingham Palace, with black and white, mahogany-panelled interiors
best_for: Travelers who want a base steps from Buckingham Palace
Couples looking for a suite under a glass ceiling
Families who want connecting rooms in a family wing

facts.text: Hotel 41 is just steps from Buckingham Palace.
The Royal Mews and The Queen's Gallery are a short walk from the hotel.
The River Thames, the Houses of Parliament, Big Ben and the London Eye are within walking distance.
Hotel 41 evokes the feel of a private members' club.
Hotel 41 occupies a former ballroom on the fifth floor of a brick-and-limestone Georgian building near St. James's Park.
Guest rooms are individually styled in a black and white theme inspired by French cartoonist Sem.
All guest rooms have mahogany panelling and marble bathrooms.
Every room has a Savoir bed.
The hotel's monochrome design is complemented by mahogany-lined walls, open fireplaces and leather furniture.
Hotel 41 offers family wings that connect several rooms with internal doors.
The Rubens at the Palace adjoins Hotel 41 and is connected to it via a concealed door.
The nearest tube station is Victoria.

highlights.text: The Conservatory Suite has a glass ceiling, so guests sleep beneath the night sky.
The Conservatory Suite has panoramic views of the London skyline.
The interiors feature prints by Rene Gruau, drawings by caricaturist Sem, antique globes and marble busts.
Under the 'plunder the pantry' concept, sweet and savoury treats are laid out daily until late, alongside a help-yourself ice cream fridge.
The Resident Manager can arrange surprises such as proposals and anniversary or birthday celebrations, plus babysitting and pet-sitting services.

considerations.text: Hotel 41's lounge and dining room is exclusively for in-house guests; for more dining options, guests use the two restaurants at the adjoining sister hotel, The Rubens at the Palace.
Interleading rooms and family wings must be booked directly through the reservations team.
WhataHotel notes compact room sizes typical of a historic London property.
